entries.title: Service failed to start
entries.what: A Windows service could not start. The message contains the error.
causes: Service is disabled or its program was uninstalled
Wrong account or expired password for the service account
fix: Open services.msc and check the service's startup type, account and dependencies
If the program was removed, set the service to Disabled or reinstall the program
For service accounts: update the stored password

entries.title: Service depends on a service that failed
entries.summary: Service "{0}" could not start because "{1}" failed
entries.what: A service could not start because a service it depends on did not start.
causes: The dependency failed first (look for its own 7000/7009/7023)
fix: Fix the dependency service first

entries.title: Service start timed out
entries.summary: Service "{1}" did not start in time
entries.what: A service did not report that it started within the timeout (usually 30 seconds).
causes: Slow boot (many startup programs, slow disk)
Service waiting for network or another service
fix: Harmless if the service is running later
Otherwise set it to Automatic (Delayed Start) or investigate the slow component

entries.title: Service did not respond in time
entries.summary: Service "{1}" did not respond to a control request in time
entries.what: A service took too long to respond to a start, stop or pause request.
fix: If it repeats, check the service's own logs and updates

entries.title: Service hung on starting
entries.what: A service started but never finished starting.
causes: Waiting for a resource that is not available
fix: Restart the service; check its own logs; update or reinstall the program

entries.title: Service terminated with an error
entries.what: A service stopped and reported an error (shown in the message).
fix: Look at the error text below
Check the service's own logs

entries.title: Service stopped with a service-specific error
entries.what: A service stopped and returned its own error code (meaning is defined by the service vendor).
fix: Search the vendor's documentation for the error code

entries.title: Boot drivers failed to load
entries.what: One or more drivers configured to start at boot did not load.
causes: Leftover driver from uninstalled software or hardware
fix: If the named driver belongs to removed software, it is usually harmless; remove it with the vendor's cleanup tool
Otherwise reinstall the related device driver

entries.title: Service crashed and was restarted
entries.summary: Service "{0}" crashed ({1|ordinal} time) - Windows restarted it
entries.what: A service ended unexpectedly; Windows ran the configured recovery action (usually a restart).
causes: Bug in the service or its program
fix: Update or reinstall the program that owns the service
Look in the Application log for a crash (Application Error 1000) at the same time - it names the faulting module

entries.title: Service recovery action failed
entries.what: Windows tried to recover a crashed service (e.g. restart it) and that failed too.
fix: Fix the underlying crash first

entries.title: Service crashed
entries.what: A service ended unexpectedly and no recovery action was configured.
causes: Bug in the service or its program
fix: Update or reinstall the program that owns the service
Check the Application log for a crash at the same time

entries.title: Service changed state
entries.what: A service started or stopped. Thousands of these are normal.

entries.title: Service start type changed
entries.summary: Start type of "{0}" changed from {1} to {2}
entries.what: A service's startup type was changed (often by Windows Update or an installer).

entries.title: Stop control sent to a service
entries.what: A stop request was sent to a service, with the reason.

entries.title: Service did not shut down properly
entries.summary: Service "{0}" did not shut down properly
entries.what: A service did not stop properly during shutdown. Can slow down shutdown.
fix: Update the program; harmless if it is rare

entries.title: New service installed
entries.what: A new service or driver was installed. Normal for software installs - and a classic persistence technique for malware.
fix: Check the service name and file path; if you do not recognise it, investigate the file (signature, VirusTotal)

entries.title: Service could not log on
entries.summary: Service "{0}" could not log on as {1}
entries.what: A service could not log on with its configured account, usually because the password changed.
causes: Service account password changed or expired
fix: Update the password on the service's Log On tab
Use a managed service account where possible

entries.title: Interactive service not supported
entries.what: A legacy service is marked as interactive, which Windows no longer supports. Usually harmless.
